{{Short description|Italian experimental physicist}}
{{COI|date=June 2013}}

'''Carlo Franzinetti''' (March 31, 1923, in [[Rome]] – November 28, 1980, in [[Llantwit Major]]) was an Italian [[experimental physicist]].<ref name=":0">Verde, Mario. ''Atti dell' Accademia delle Scienze di Torino. ''Torino: L' Accademia, 1980-81. Print.

(With Thanks to Maria Itala Ferrero and Alberta Marzari Chiesa)</ref>
[[File:Carlo Franzinetti.jpg|thumb|Carlo Franzinetti]]

==Personal biography==
Carlo Franzinetti was born in [[Rome]], son of Guido Franzinetti, a music critic, and Ada Guastalla, a mathematician and linguist.<ref name=":1">Bemporad, Carlo. ''Ricordo di Carlo Franzinetti (1923-1980)''.http://www.df.unipi.it/~rossi/M_franzinetti.pdf</ref> He was married to Prof. Joan Rees.<ref name=":0" />

During the German occupation of Italy, he was an active member in  Resistance Movement. He was one of the leaders of a student group of anti-fascist activists that included [[Carlo Lizzani]], [[:it:Maurizio Ferrara|Maurizio Ferrara]], [[:it:Dario Puccini|Dario Puccini]], and other important figures in the development of post-war Italy.<ref>Pavia, Aldo. ''La Resistenza a Roma''</ref>

He graduated from the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]] "[[La Sapienza]]" in physics with a [[thesis]] about projects of construction of an [[isotope separator]] based on [[thermophoresis]].

His professional scientific career started when he was 25 (8 May 1948), when he published the article "Emission of Li8 in the Explosive Disintegration of Nuclei" with [[R.M. Payne]] in the science journal ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]''.<ref name=":0" /><ref>C. Franzinetti and R.M. Payne. Emission of Li8 in the Explosive Disintegration of Nuclei, ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' 161. 8 May 1948</ref>

==Cosmic radiation research==

In 1947 he joined the [[University of Bristol]] as a research assistant at the [[H.H. Wills Physical Laboratory]], under the guidance of [[Nobel Prize in Physics|Nobel Laureate]] Prof. [[C. F. Powell]]. Powell's team's research looked at the sub-nuclear structure of matter through the study of [[cosmic rays]] with [[nuclear emulsion]].<ref name=":0" />

In 1950 he returned to Rome but he continued his study of cosmic rays. One of the ideas that came out of Powell's team was an expedition in the [[Mediterranean region]] to study cosmic radiation at [[high atmosphere]] (25 to 30&nbsp;km) using [[Aerostat|aerostatic balloons]] carrying [[photographic emulsion]]. Carlo followed the expedition, which took place during the summers of 1952 and 1953 in [[Naples]] and in [[Cagliari]], with researchers and students from 13 different physics institutes from various countries. Thirteen balloons were launched, 3 of which were test balloons. Of the other ten, 7 were recovered and 40% of the emulsions had been exposed to cosmic radiation.<ref name=":3">''European Council for Nuclear Research Report on the Expedition to the Central Mediterranean for the Study of Cosmic Radiation''. Rome, 30 September 1952.  https://cds.cern.ch/record/21571/files/CM-P00075414-e.pdf</ref>

==Study of neutrinos==

In 1962 he began working in [[Geneva]] as a senior physicist at the [[European Organization for Nuclear Research]] (CERN).<ref name=":1" /> During his time there he played a key role in promoting and working with the Heavy Liquid Bubble Chamber, [[Gargamelle]],<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |last=Krige |first=J. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gQbgQrYlpIoC&dq=franzinetti&pg=PA41 |title=History of CERN, III |date=1996-12-18 |publisher=Elsevier |isbn=978-0-08-053403-9 |language=en}}</ref> where he also conducted his studies of [[neutrino]]s. The first report for the request of a common European Heavy Liquid Chamber at CERN was submitted by [[:fr:André Lagarrigue|André Lagarrigue]] but, needing the support of Italian and possibly [[United Kingdom|British]] physicists, he contacted Franzinetti. Franzinetti led the Italian group concerned with the proposal and construction of the Heavy Liquid Chamber, Gargamelle.<ref name=":2" /> At CERN he studied, at different energies, with neutrino and [[antineutrino]] beams, on different kinds of targets, the production of [[pions]] and [[strange particles]], [[Elastic interaction|elastic]] and quasi-elastic interactions, and, through analysis of the interactions of Neutrinos, he studied the form factors of [[nucleons]].<ref name=":0" />

==Biophysics==

His interest in [[biophysics]] started during his time in Pisa. During his time in [[Turin]] he led a biophysics team of students from the Universities of Turin and Pisa, which conducted studies on [[visual perception]]. He followed students alongside [[:it:Giuseppe Moruzzi|Giuseppe Moruzzi]], a [[physiologist]] at the University of Pisa.<ref name=":4">''La Fisica pisana dopo la Seconda Guerra Mondiale (1947-1982)''</ref>

==Chronology==

*Born in Rome on March 31, 1923.<ref name=":0" />

[[File:Carlo Franzinetti e Bruno Pontecorvo.jpg|thumb|Carlo Franzinetti (Left) and [[Bruno Pontecorvo]] (Right)]]

*In 1943–1944, he was active in the Roman Resistance and in hiding from the [[Nazi]]-[[Fascist]] regime.<ref name=":4" />
*In 1945 he completed his degree in [[Physics]] at the University of Rome, at age 22, and started his research career in [[Rome]] working for the [[Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche]].<ref name=":0" />
*In 1947-1950 he worked as a research assistant at the [[University of Bristol]].<ref name=":0" />
*In 1951 he married Joan Rees.<ref name=":0" />
*In 1951-1958 he worked as an assistant professor at the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]].
*In the summers of 1952 and 1953 he took part in cosmic radiation study expeditions in the Mediterranean.<ref name=":3" />
*In 1956 he was granted the title of Libero Docente ([[Habilitation]]).
*In 1958 he was a physics professor at the [[University of Trieste]], and from 1959 to 1966 he held the chair in Structure of Matter at the [[University of Pisa]].<ref>Kay, Ernest. Dictionary of International Biography, Volume 14. Cambridge: International Biographical Center, 1978. Print.</ref>
*In 1962 he began working as a senior physicist at [[CERN]].<ref name=":0" />
*From 1966 on, he held the chair of [[particle physics]] at the [[University of Turin]].<ref name=":0" />
*He moved to [[Llantwit Major]] in 1980, where he died on November 28, 1980.

==Honors==
*''Borsa di Studio Carlo Franzinetti.'' On his death, [[INFN]] ([[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare|Istituto Nazionale di FIsica Nucleare]]), instituted a scholarship in his name which was won by Claudio Santoni.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.protrevi.com/protrevi/SantN12X15.asp |title=Trevi Premia Claudio Santoni - rass. Stampa |accessdate=2013-07-04 |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304000833/http://www.protrevi.com/protrevi/SantN12X15.asp |archive-date=2016-03-04 }}</ref>
*''Aula Carlo Franzinetti''. Lecture hall named in honor of Carlo Franzinetti at the University of Turin in the Institute of Physics<ref>Maria Itala Ferrero and Alberta Marzari Chiesa. ''Ricordo di Carlo Franzinetti In occasione dell' inaugurazione dell' aula del Dipartimento di Fisica Sperimentale a lui dedicata. ''Turin.</ref>
